| [CASE-371](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-371.md) | Toy transformer forgetting study | A toy-scale stand-in for [CASE-274](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-274.md)'s design, for [LEAD-043](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-043.md). numpy only, CPU, about two hours of compute on a shared machine. A two-layer transformer (d 64, 4 heads, no layer norm, hand-written backward pass) memorizes 256 random facts under two query templates. 32 target facts are then fine-tuned away in seven arms: unlearning toward a uniform output, gradient ascent and overwriting with new values, each at one cue or two, with rehearsal of the rest; and an unrelated new task without rehearsal. Every model has a twin trained from the same initialization on a world that differs only in the target values, so every readout has a false-positive rate. Pooled over 4 seeds and both worlds, in the unlearning, overwriting and new-task arms 87 to 98 percent of the forgotten facts are recovered by at least one reader, against 28 to 46 percent for the twin's values, and the average fact is recovered by 2.8 to 3.6 readers against 0.4 to 1.0. An untrained cue recovers 73 to 79 percent when one cue was fine-tuned; reverting one early block's update restores 41 to 55 percent; relearning half the targets makes the second fine-tuned-away value faster to learn after overwriting or a new task (8 to 8.5 steps against 17.5 to 25.5 for the twin). Gradient ascent instead collapses the model (retained facts at 8 to 19 percent), and run past its criterion leaves no reader above baseline. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [CASE-374](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-374.md) | Assembly chain with two alternative seams | [LEAD-116](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-116.md) asked that [CASE-219](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-219.md)'s stochastic assembly study and its factorial variant [CASE-220](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-220.md) be run, extending [CASE-216](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-216.md)'s annealing toy, and the intermediates scored by the committor q(s) = Pr_s(tau_F < tau_K). The model is a continuous-time Markov chain whose state is the set of bonds formed (a subset of four), with two alternative seams a and b each nucleating a shared body c, d into two valid folds F_A and F_B, an incompatible-seam trap (both seams) and an unnucleated collapse (a seamless assembly), the two traps taken from Dunn et al. and from DeLuca et al. / Sobczak. Committors are exact linear solves. Each seam alone is a productive nucleus (q from 0.19 to 0.81) but both together are a trap (0.04): an assembly-dynamics instance of [CLAIM-599](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-599.md)'s non-monotone V, which had only a stipulated example. The committor ranks a one-bond nucleus (0.81) above the four-bond misfolded state (0.05), so it orders intermediates by their future not their extent, as [CLAIM-567](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-567.md) separates reachable from reliably reached. Targeted early stabilisation of one designed seam is productive (Delta_q_N about +0.6) and of both a trap (-0.18), [CASE-220](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-220.md)'s factorial 2x2. At fixed total stock, moving the seam budget from a to b slides the realised share of F_A from 1.00 to 0.00 with the attainable set unchanged ([QUESTION-400](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-400.md)). A fold is reached far more often than it persists ([CLAIM-566](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-566.md)). The model and its rates are the assistant's and invented. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-389](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-389.md) | Seed sets in kinetic constraint growth | [QUESTION-380](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-380.md) asks for a predictor, computed from a constraint architecture, of which local subsystems raise or lower the chance of a coherent global organization, tested in a system other than the one it was built for; UFI, the folding-island predictor of Stern, Pinson and Murugan ([THEORY-1418](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1418.md)), cannot flag a superset that lowers the chance. A race reading of folding islands (VIC: a component counts only if the first seed front to reach it forces it) and an alternative (ICN: island coverage per disconnected nucleus) were pre-registered and tested on a kinetic constraint-growth model in the threshold-2 regime of the kinetic tile assembly model ([THEORY-1451](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1451.md)). Adding a seed already in its target state can halve the chance of exact assembly (38 of 40 significant decreases confirmed with 3000 runs), and island coverage predicts the chance better than the number of seeds. Neither VIC nor ICN transfers: VIC ranks seed sets worse than the monotone island union (Spearman 0.22 against 0.54) and flags 193 additions as harmful of which 2 are. The harmful seeds have large islands; the errors are order effects at the binding threshold. A post hoc predictor, threshold-front forcing (TFF), meets the pre-registered criterion on five fresh architectures (Spearman 0.64 against 0.48, AUC 0.94, recall 0.66, precision 0.11). The model is the assistant's. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

Place there is confounded with conditionality. No case tests whether adding an intervention can make an organization fail. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
